unit.label: Distance and two actions
unit.title: Near the Noodle Shop
unit.description: Read the end of the trip, do two things at once, and describe distance.

goal.text: 他們一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖。
goal.pinyin: Tāmen yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú.
goal.meaning: They eat noodles while looking at the map.

lessons.title: Ready for noodles
lessons.subtitle: Be hungry and find a noodle shop.

steps.prompt: What does 餓 mean here?
steps.explanation: 餓 (è) means hungry. 我有一點餓。 (Wǒ yǒu yìdiǎn è.) means “I am a little hungry.” 有一點 softens the degree; 我餓了 (wǒ è le) says “I am hungry now.”

steps.prompt: What does 麵店 mean here?
steps.explanation: 麵店 (miàn diàn) means noodle shop: 麵 is noodles and 店 is shop. 我們去麵店吃麵。 (Wǒmen qù miàn diàn chī miàn.) means “We go to a noodle shop to eat noodles.”

steps.prompt: 覺得有點餓，去哪裡吃麵？
steps.explanation: In this context, 麵店

lessons.title: Two things at once
lessons.subtitle: Describe simultaneous actions with 一邊…一邊….

steps.prompt: What does 一邊 mean here?
steps.explanation: In this lesson 一邊 (yìbiān) introduces an action happening at the same time as another. Repeat it before both actions: 一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖 (yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú), “eat noodles while looking at the map.” It does not mean first do one, then the other.

steps.prompt: 我一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖。 — what does the whole sentence mean?
options: I eat noodles while looking at the map.
I look at the map only after I eat.
I eat only after putting away the map.
steps.answer: I eat noodles while looking at the map.
steps.explanation: 一邊 (yìbiān) comes before each of two actions performed by the same person at the same time. Both action phrases follow the shared subject. 不可以 or 不要 before the pattern forbids the combination; 沒 before the pattern says the actions did not happen together. Add 好不好 after the two actions to propose doing them together. This pattern does not mean first one action and then the other.

steps.prompt: Interpret the full message: 他們一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖。
options: They eat noodles while looking at the map.
They look at the map after eating noodles.
They eat noodles without looking at the map.
steps.answer: They eat noodles while looking at the map.
steps.explanation: Put 一邊 before 吃麵 and repeat 一邊 before 看地圖. The same people do both actions at the same time. Both copies are needed in this full pattern.

steps.prompt: 一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖。 When are these actions done?
steps.explanation: In this context, At the same time.

steps.prompt: 不要一邊走路，一邊看手機。 What is discouraged?
options: Looking at a phone while walking.
Walking after putting the phone away.
Looking at a phone while sitting.
steps.answer: Looking at a phone while walking.
steps.explanation: 不要 forbids the two actions happening together.

steps.prompt: 我們一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖，好不好？ What is proposed?
options: Looking at the map while eating noodles.
Looking at the map after finishing the noodles.
Finishing the map before starting the noodles.
steps.answer: Looking at the map while eating noodles.
steps.explanation: 好不好 asks agreement to the simultaneous actions.

lessons.title: How far is it?
lessons.subtitle: Locate a store using 離…不遠.

steps.prompt: What does 離 mean here?
steps.explanation: 離 (lí) marks the reference place when stating distance. 學校離這裡很近。 (Xuéxiào lí zhèlǐ hěn jìn.) means “The school is close to here.” Name the place being located, then 離 + reference place, then 很近 or 很遠.

steps.prompt: 郵局離學校很近。 — what does the whole sentence mean?
options: The post office is close to the school.
The post office is far from the school.
The school is inside the post office.
steps.answer: The post office is close to the school.
steps.explanation: Place A + 離 + place B + 遠/近 describes the distance between two places. B is the reference point. 很近 means close and 不遠 means not far. Put 不 before the distance word, not before 離. To ask, say 遠不遠 or 是不是很遠. Unlike 從, which gives the start of movement, 離 measures distance without saying that anyone moves.

steps.prompt: What does 麵店離學校不遠。 mean?
options: The noodle shop is not far from school.
The noodle shop is far from school.
The noodle shop is inside the school.
steps.answer: The noodle shop is not far from school.
steps.explanation: 麵店 is the place being located; 離學校 means “from the school.” 不遠 means “not far.” Put 不 before 遠, not before 離.

steps.prompt: 麵店離學校不遠。 Which word is negated?
steps.explanation: In this context, 遠

steps.prompt: 麵店離學校遠不遠？ What is being asked?
options: Whether the noodle shop is far from school.
Which way to walk to school.
Whether the noodle shop is inside the school.
steps.answer: Whether the noodle shop is far from school.
steps.explanation: 遠不遠 asks about distance. 離學校 gives the reference place.

steps.prompt: You want to say the noodle shop is not far from school. Which sentence works?
steps.explanation: Negate 遠 with 不遠. Keep 離學校 together as the reference-place phrase.

lessons.title: A backpack at the right time
lessons.subtitle: Describe what you happen to want.

steps.prompt: What does 背包 mean here?
steps.explanation: 背包 (bēibāo) means backpack. Read 背 as first-tone bēi in this word. 我想買一個背包。 (Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí ge bēibāo.) means “I want to buy a backpack.” Use 個 to count backpacks.

steps.prompt: What does 正好 mean here?
steps.explanation: 正好 (zhènghǎo) here means happen to or just at the right time. 我正好想買背包。 (Wǒ zhènghǎo xiǎng mǎi bēibāo.) means “I happen to want to buy a backpack.” 正好 goes before 想買 and connects the wish to the present opportunity.

steps.prompt: What does 我正好想買一個背包。 mean?
options: I happen to want to buy a backpack.
I have already bought a backpack.
I happen to want to sell a backpack.
steps.answer: I happen to want to buy a backpack.
steps.explanation: 正好 goes before 想買 to say the wish fits the present opportunity. 一個背包 means one backpack; 想買 expresses a wish, not an already completed purchase.

steps.prompt: 正好想買背包 describes what?
steps.explanation: In this context, Happening to want a backpack.

lessons.title: Pens and a notebook
lessons.subtitle: Count stationery with the right measure words.

steps.prompt: What does 筆 mean here?
steps.explanation: 筆 (bǐ) means pen or writing instrument. 我想買筆。 (Wǒ xiǎng mǎi bǐ.) means “I want to buy pens.” The next card teaches how to count them.

steps.prompt: What does 枝 mean here?
steps.explanation: 枝 (zhī) is the measure word for pens here. 一枝筆 (yì zhī bǐ) is one pen; 兩枝筆 (liǎng zhī bǐ) is two pens. The order is number + 枝 + 筆. 枝 counts the items; 筆 names them.

steps.prompt: What does 本子 mean here?
steps.explanation: 本子 (běnzi) means notebook. 一本本子 (yì běn běnzi) is one notebook. The first 本 is the measure word for books; the 本 in 本子 is part of the noun. Keep both: 一 + 本 + 本子.

steps.prompt: What does 她買了兩枝筆和一本本子。 mean?
options: She bought two pens and one notebook.
She bought two notebooks and one pen.
She wants to buy two pens but has not bought them.
steps.answer: She bought two pens and one notebook.
steps.explanation: 兩枝筆 counts pens with 枝. 一本本子 counts a notebook with 本; 本子 is the noun. 和 joins both things bought.

steps.prompt: Which phrase counts two pens?
steps.explanation: In this context, 兩枝筆

lessons.title: Finally, on Shida Road
lessons.subtitle: Describe the final purchases and a location on Shida Road.

steps.prompt: What does 最後 mean here?
steps.explanation: 最後 (zuìhòu) means finally or in the end. 最後她買了兩枝筆。 (Zuìhòu tā mǎi le liǎng zhī bǐ.) means “Finally she bought two pens.” 最後 puts this event at the end of a sequence.

steps.prompt: What does 師大路上 mean here?
steps.explanation: 師大路上 (Shīdà Lù shàng) means on Shida Road. 師大路 is the road name and 上 locates something along it. 師大路上有很多店。 (Shīdà Lù shàng yǒu hěn duō diàn.) means “There are many shops on Shida Road.” It does not mean inside the university.

steps.prompt: Interpret the full message: 最後她買了兩枝筆和一本本子。
options: Finally she bought two pens and one notebook.
Finally she bought one pen and two notebooks.
Finally she bought two notebooks and two pens.
steps.answer: Finally she bought two pens and one notebook.
steps.explanation: 最後 means finally. 買了 marks the purchase. 兩枝筆 is two pens; 一本本子 is one notebook. 和 joins the two purchases. Use 枝 for pens and 本 for notebooks.

steps.prompt: 最後他們在師大路上買了東西。 Which part marks the end of events?
steps.explanation: In this context, 最後

steps.prompt: 他買了一個背包。她買了兩枝筆和一本本子。 What did the woman buy?
steps.explanation: 她 marks the woman; her purchases follow 買了. The backpack belongs to the man in the first sentence.

b2u4-l2-simultaneous.title: Two actions at the same time

Both action phrases follow the shared subject. 不可以 or 不要 before the pattern forbids the combination; 沒 before the pattern says the actions did not happen together. examples.meaning: He did not look at the map while eating noodles.

b2u4-l2-simultaneous.remember: Both actions overlap; keep both 一邊 parts.

b2u4-l3-distance.title: Distance between two places: 離
b2u4-l3-distance.pattern: place A + 離 + place B + distance (遠/近)
b2u4-l3-distance.explanation: Place A + 離 + place B + 遠/近 describes the distance between two places. B is the reference point. 很近 means close and 不遠 means not far. Put 不 before the distance word, not before 離. To ask, say 遠不遠 or 是不是很遠. Unlike 從, which gives the start of movement, 離 measures distance without saying that anyone moves.

examples.meaning: The post office is close to the school.
The noodle shop is not far from school.

examples.pinyin: Miàndiàn lí xuéxiào yuǎn bu yuǎn?
examples.meaning: Is the noodle shop far from school?

b2u4-l3-distance.remember: Negate or question 遠/近, not 離.

b2u4-l1-word-1.note: 餓 (è) means hungry. 我有一點餓。 (Wǒ yǒu yìdiǎn è.) means “I am a little hungry.” 有一點 softens the degree; 我餓了 (wǒ è le) says “I am hungry now.”

b2u4-l1-word-2.note: 麵店 (miàn diàn) means noodle shop: 麵 is noodles and 店 is shop. 我們去麵店吃麵。 (Wǒmen qù miàn diàn chī miàn.) means “We go to a noodle shop to eat noodles.”

b2u4-l2-word-1.note: In this lesson 一邊 (yìbiān) introduces an action happening at the same time as another. Repeat it before both actions: 一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖 (yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú), “eat noodles while looking at the map.” It does not mean first do one, then the other.

b2u4-l2-model.text: 他們一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖。
b2u4-l2-model.pinyin: Tāmen yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú.
b2u4-l2-model.meaning: They eat noodles while looking at the map.
b2u4-l2-model.note: Put 一邊 before 吃麵 and repeat 一邊 before 看地圖. The same people do both actions at the same time. Both copies are needed in this full pattern.

b2u4-l3-word-1.note: 離 (lí) marks the reference place when stating distance. 學校離這裡很近。 (Xuéxiào lí zhèlǐ hěn jìn.) means “The school is close to here.” Name the place being located, then 離 + reference place, then 很近 or 很遠.

b2u4-l3-model.meaning: The noodle shop is not far from school.
b2u4-l3-model.note: 麵店 is the place being located; 離學校 means “from the school.” 不遠 means “not far.” Put 不 before 遠, not before 離.

b2u4-l4-word-1.note: 背包 (bēibāo) means backpack. Read 背 as first-tone bēi in this word. 我想買一個背包。 (Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí ge bēibāo.) means “I want to buy a backpack.” Use 個 to count backpacks.

b2u4-l4-word-2.note: 正好 (zhènghǎo) here means happen to or just at the right time. 我正好想買背包。 (Wǒ zhènghǎo xiǎng mǎi bēibāo.) means “I happen to want to buy a backpack.” 正好 goes before 想買 and connects the wish to the present opportunity.

b2u4-l4-model.pinyin: Wǒ zhènghǎo xiǎng mǎi yí ge bēibāo.
b2u4-l4-model.meaning: I happen to want to buy a backpack.
b2u4-l4-model.note: 正好 goes before 想買 to say the wish fits the present opportunity. 一個背包 means one backpack; 想買 expresses a wish, not an already completed purchase.

b2u4-l5-word-1.note: 筆 (bǐ) means pen or writing instrument. 我想買筆。 (Wǒ xiǎng mǎi bǐ.) means “I want to buy pens.” The next card teaches how to count them.

b2u4-l5-word-2.note: 枝 (zhī) is the measure word for pens here. 一枝筆 (yì zhī bǐ) is one pen; 兩枝筆 (liǎng zhī bǐ) is two pens. The order is number + 枝 + 筆. 枝 counts the items; 筆 names them.

b2u4-l5-word-3.note: 本子 (běnzi) means notebook. 一本本子 (yì běn běnzi) is one notebook. The first 本 is the measure word for books; the 本 in 本子 is part of the noun. Keep both: 一 + 本 + 本子.

b2u4-l5-model.text: 她買了兩枝筆和一本本子。
b2u4-l5-model.pinyin: Tā mǎi le liǎng zhī bǐ hé yì běn běnzi.
b2u4-l5-model.meaning: She bought two pens and one notebook.
b2u4-l5-model.note: 兩枝筆 counts pens with 枝. 一本本子 counts a notebook with 本; 本子 is the noun. 和 joins both things bought.

b2u4-l6-word-1.note: 最後 (zuìhòu) means finally or in the end. 最後她買了兩枝筆。 (Zuìhòu tā mǎi le liǎng zhī bǐ.) means “Finally she bought two pens.” 最後 puts this event at the end of a sequence.

b2u4-l6-word-2.note: 師大路上 (Shīdà Lù shàng) means on Shida Road. 師大路 is the road name and 上 locates something along it. 師大路上有很多店。 (Shīdà Lù shàng yǒu hěn duō diàn.) means “There are many shops on Shida Road.” It does not mean inside the university.

b2u4-l6-model.text: 最後她買了兩枝筆和一本本子。
b2u4-l6-model.pinyin: Zuìhòu tā mǎi le liǎng zhī bǐ hé yì běn běnzi.
b2u4-l6-model.meaning: Finally she bought two pens and one notebook.
b2u4-l6-model.note: 最後 means finally. 買了 marks the purchase. 兩枝筆 is two pens; 一本本子 is one notebook. 和 joins the two purchases. Use 枝 for pens and 本 for notebooks.

b2u4-l7-cumulative-1.text: 他們一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖。
b2u4-l7-cumulative-1.pinyin: Tāmen yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú.
b2u4-l7-cumulative-1.meaning: They eat noodles while looking at the map.
b2u4-l7-cumulative-1.note: Put 一邊 before 吃麵 and repeat 一邊 before 看地圖. The same people do both actions at the same time. Both copies are needed in this full pattern.

b2u4-l7-cumulative-2.meaning: The noodle shop is not far from school.
b2u4-l7-cumulative-2.note: 麵店 is the place being located; 離學校 means “from the school.” 不遠 means “not far.” Put 不 before 遠, not before 離.

b2u4-l7-cumulative-3.text: 最後她買了兩枝筆和一本本子。
b2u4-l7-cumulative-3.pinyin: Zuìhòu tā mǎi le liǎng zhī bǐ hé yì běn běnzi.
b2u4-l7-cumulative-3.meaning: Finally she bought two pens and one notebook.
b2u4-l7-cumulative-3.note: 最後 means finally. 買了 marks the purchase. 兩枝筆 is two pens; 一本本子 is one notebook. 和 joins the two purchases. Use 枝 for pens and 本 for notebooks.

b2u4-shopping-context.text: 他們一邊吃麵，一邊看地圖。他正好想買背包，最後買了一個。她買了兩枝筆和一本本子。
b2u4-shopping-context.pinyin: Tāmen yìbiān chī miàn, yìbiān kàn dìtú. Tā zhènghǎo xiǎng mǎi bēibāo, zuìhòu mǎi le yí ge. Tā mǎi le liǎng zhī bǐ hé yì běn běnzi.
b2u4-shopping-context.meaning: They look at the map while eating noodles. He happens to want a backpack and finally buys one. She buys two pens and one notebook.
b2u4-shopping-context.note: The first sentence describes simultaneous actions. 他 then refers to the male shopper and 她 to the female shopper. 一個 refers back to the backpack; 枝 counts pens and 本 counts notebooks. This is the complete practice passage.
